That's actually the normal behavior, not a bug. By default, React re-renders every child whenever its parent re-renders — it doesn't check if the props are the same.

To stop that, wrap the child in `React.memo`. That tells React to skip the re-render if the props haven't changed.

But watch out for one trap: if any of the props are functions, objects, or arrays written inline (like `onClick={() => ...}` or `style={{ color: 'red' }}`), React sees a brand new one on every render, even if the values look identical. So `memo` won't help unless you also wrap those with `useCallback` or `useMemo` in the parent.

Also worth checking: if the child reads from a Context, it re-renders whenever that context's value changes, no matter what props you pass.
